key_insight: In a head-to-head benchmark, specialized open-source thigh muscle MRI segmentation models generally outperformed foundation and general-purpose architectures, especially on harder pathological scans.
clinical_relevance: Better segmentation can improve MRI-based muscle volume, radiomics, and fat-fraction measurements, but performance variability means tool choice can materially affect research and clinical interpretation.
method: Compared 8 open-source segmentation tools on 3D thigh MRI.
Used 3 base datasets and later derived datasets for broader testing.
Evaluated both quantitative accuracy and qualitative usability.
evidence_signal: The study found substantial performance differences across methods and datasets, with many algorithms dropping in accuracy on pathological cases.
watch_item: Results may not generalize well to underrepresented populations or pathologies, so deployment needs careful local validation.
paper_title: Benchmarking open-source automated thigh muscle MRI segmentation algorithms
